question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s tight grip on the Chinese Communist Party’s key institutions, including the Politburo Standing Committee, Central Military Commission, and security apparatus, underpins trader expectations that he will remain paramount leader through 2026. Since abolishing presidential term limits in 2018 and securing a third term in 2022–2023, Xi has installed loyalists across senior posts while conducting ongoing rectification and anti-corruption drives that have neutralized potential rivals without triggering open factional conflict. No verified health incidents, public challenges, or leadership signals have emerged in 2026 to alter this trajectory ahead of the 21st Party Congress expected in late 2027. Although sudden illness, elite realignment, or unforeseen domestic crises could theoretically shift outcomes, the current absence of succession planning or visible opposition sustains the market’s strong consensus against removal before 2027.

question: Will Gavin Newsom win the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the named individual wins and accepts the 2028 nomination of the Democratic Party for U.S. president. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Democratic presidential nomination for 2028 remains wide open more than two years before the convention, producing a tight cluster of trader probabilities among multiple contenders with no one exceeding 20 percent. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Gavin Newsom, and Jon Ossoff lead the field at 19.9 percent, 15.8 percent, and 13.7 percent respectively, while Kamala Harris and others sit further back, reflecting an extended window for fundraising, coalition building, and positioning by senators, governors, and House members. The absence of an early consensus arises from the long timeline before primaries, allowing diverse ideological and regional factions within the party to test support. Midterm results, early-state polling, endorsements, and major policy debates could create separation by clarifying which candidates demonstrate stronger appeal across swing-state electorates and broader party networks.
